title: Privacy & Security Covenants — Short-Form Agreement for SMB Customers (Template)
content:
Purpose:
This short-form Privacy & Security Covenants document is intended for use as an accompanying exhibit to a Master Services Agreement (MSA) for small-to-medium business (SMB) customers of Redwood Inference. It provides a concise, readily negotiable set of data processing and security commitments suitable for customers who require clear protections without a multi-page DPA negotiation.

Instructions to drafter: replace bracketed placeholders with customer/vendor names, select applicable deployment mode (Hosted API | Dedicated | Private), and strike optional provisions as agreed. This template is deliberately concise; for enterprise or regulated customers, use the full DPA appendix instead.

1. Parties and Scope
1.1 Parties: This Exhibit ("Covenants") is between [Customer Name] ("Customer") and Redwood Inference, Inc. ("Redwood" or "Vendor").
1.2 Scope: These Covenants govern processing of Customer Data (defined below) by Redwood in connection with the provision of Redwood's inference services under the MSA, including Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment options.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Customer Data" means any data, content, prompts, files, or model inputs provided by or on behalf of Customer to Redwood for the purpose of using Redwood services, and any outputs generated by Redwood at Customer's direction to the extent the MSA assigns Customer ownership.
2.2 "Personal Data" means Customer Data that qualifies as personal data under applicable law.
2.3 "Subprocessor" means any third party engaged by Redwood to process Customer Data.

3. Processing and Purpose
3.1 Processing: Redwood will process Customer Data only to provide the services described in the MSA and for no other purpose, except as legally required.
3.2 Instructions: Redwood will act only on Customer's documented instructions with respect to Personal Data, subject to the MSA.

4. Security Measures
4.1 Baseline Controls: Redwood will maintain administrative, technical, and physical safeguards appropriate to the processing and the risk, including: access control and role-based permissions, encryption at rest and in transit, logging and monitoring, vulnerability management, and periodic security assessments.
4.2 Encryption and Keys: For Hosted and Dedicated offerings, Redwood encrypts Customer Data in transit (TLS 1.2+). Customer Data at rest is encrypted using vendor-managed keys by default. Upon request and subject to a separate agreement, Redwood supports Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) for Dedicated and Private deployments.
4.3 Least Privilege: Access to Customer Data is limited to personnel with a business need; emergency access is logged and reviewed.

5. Subprocessors
5.1 Notice: Redwood maintains a current list of categories of Subprocessors and will provide Customer with prior notice of any material changes.
5.2 Liability: Redwood remains responsible for acts and omissions of Subprocessors to the extent required by applicable law and the MSA.

6. Incident Response and Notification
6.1 Incident Handling: Redwood maintains an incident response program and will investigate security incidents affecting Customer Data.
6.2 Notification Timeline: If Redwood becomes aware of a security incident resulting in unauthorized access to Customer Data, Redwood will notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within 72 hours of confirming a breach that materially affects Customer Data, unless prohibited by law. Notices will include nature of incident, scope, mitigation steps, and recommended Customer actions.

7. Data Retention, Deletion, and Return
7.1 Retention: Redwood will retain Customer Data only as long as necessary to provide the Services and as required by the MSA or applicable law.
7.2 Deletion: Upon termination or expiration of the MSA, Redwood will, at Customer's election, return Customer Data or securely delete it within 30 days, except for backups which will be deleted within 90 days.
7.3 Anonymization Option: Where feasible, Redwood may offer a one-way anonymization service on request to assist with data minimization.

8. Access, Audit Rights, and Evidence
8.1 Self-Service Evidence: Redwood provides Customers with operational evidence (e.g., encryption status, audit logs excerpts, pen test summaries) via the Redwood Console or upon request.
8.2 Remote Audit: For SMB customers, formal on-site audits are excluded. Customer may request a short remote evidence package and a SOC 2 summary report subject to confidentiality terms and a reasonable administrative fee.

9. Data Residency
9.1 Region Controls: Where Customer orders a region-specific deployment, Redwood will process and store Customer Data in the selected region(s) to the extent commercially reasonable. Specific residency guarantees require Dedicated or Private deployment and may be subject to additional fees.

10. Confidentiality and Personnel
10.1 Confidentiality: Redwood and Customer each agree to keep Customer Data confidential and not disclose it except as permitted by the MSA or required by law.
10.2 Personnel: Redwood will require employees and contractors with access to Customer Data to be bound by confidentiality obligations.

11. Warranty and Liability
11.1 Security Warranty: Redwood warrants that it will implement and maintain the security measures described in Section 4.
11.2 Limitation of Liability: Except for willful misconduct or violations of data protection laws, liability for breaches of these Covenants is limited to the liability cap set out in the MSA (or, absent an MSA cap, to the amount paid by Customer in the prior 12 months).

12. Law Enforcement and Legal Requests
12.1 Legal Requests: Redwood will notify Customer of any legal requests for Customer Data unless prohibited by law or court order and will cooperate with Customer's reasonable requests to resist or limit disclosure.

13. Changes to These Covenants
13.1 Updates: Redwood may update these Covenants to reflect changes in law or service offerings. For Hosted customers, material changes will be communicated 30 days prior to taking effect and Customer will have the option to terminate affected services if material changes are unacceptable.

14. Termination and Survival
14.1 Survival: Sections 4, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12, and this Section 14 survive termination or expiration of the MSA with respect to Customer Data processed prior to termination.

15. Signatures
By signing below the parties agree that these Covenants form part of the governing agreement between Customer and Redwood for the Services.

Notes and negotiation guidance (non-binding):
- For SMB customers, prefer Customer-managed keys as an optional add-on rather than default.
- Limit remote audit scope to verification of controls (not raw data access).
- Consider adding a short section referencing model output ownership if Customer needs explicit ownership of generated outputs.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments include an appendix for on-premise evidence and change-control procedures.

Version history: Short-form v1.0 — initial draft for SMB sales and resale partners.
